levelup.name: LevelUp
levelup.desc: A clip-on bubble level for barbells, built to improve your gym performances with leveled exercises.

notipclip.name: No-Tip-Clip
notipclip.desc: An anti-tip caster for wheelchairs carrying halo-traction patients at Shriners Children’s.

slidemaster.name: Slide Master
slidemaster.desc: A wheelchair-to-shower transfer board that uses sliding mechanism to prevent skin injury in patients.

gamejam.name: Northwestern Game Jam
gamejam.desc: A horror game built in Unity: A college amateur exorcist hired to cleanse a haunted show home, only to uncover the unsettling story of its former resident.

giftme.name: GiftMe
giftme.desc: An iOS app for saving what you want into wishlists friends and family can see — idea to App Store in two months.
giftme.take: A beta of 13 friends and family shaped the UI before launch. The idea came from our own frustration with gift-giving.

plu.name: People Like Us
plu.desc: Brand system for a Copenhagen brewery where most staff are neurodivergent

neighbors.name: Neighbors
neighbors.desc: A VR film. You cannot cut. You can only wait.
neighbors.take: In VR the edit is the viewer.

scenic.name: Hidden Treasure
scenic.desc: A 3 m × 6 m mobile reveal wall for a student production: a cardboard exterior tears open to a fake-cash cavity backed by projection cloth.
scenic.take: Plautus’s Aulularia nested inside a contemporary Shanghai developer story — two worlds, one wall.

onebirth.name: One Birth Too Many
onebirth.desc: A Twine game set in a 1983 Chinese village under the One-Child Policy. One Friday morning, six perspectives, one dinner table.
onebirth.take: Choices in one character’s morning silently change another’s. You find out at dinner.

austin.name: Austin Vaccine Siting
austin.desc: Clustered 44 Austin ZIP areas to site vaccine distribution: k-medoids first, then two Gurobi integer programs.
austin.take: We handed back two answers and said which one to pick depending on what you care about.

alv.name: CASE × Ama La Vida
alv.desc: Pricing and retention strategy for a virtual career-coaching company, from five years of churn data.
alv.take: Members kept stepping down to cheaper plans. We raised the ceiling and rewarded staying up.

yello.name: CASE × Yello
yello.desc: Mapped the HR-tech landscape for a campus-recruiting platform and picked partners it could grow with.
yello.take: 98.8% of the Fortune 500 already run an ATS. The opening isn’t displacement, it’s adjacency.

amg.name: AMG-786
amg.desc: Financial analysis of a drug candidate: development costs, pricing, ten years of sales and NPV.
amg.take: “Proceed, but wary of Phase II.” I priced it against Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and Ozempic.

bike-caliper.name: Nylon Bike Caliper
bike-caliper.desc: Nylon rear brake caliper arms, 47.7% lighter on the second print, and a lesson in leverage.
bike-caliper.take: Lighter arms flexed more, but the hand force barely moved: only the lever ratio could fix that.

peek-a-boo-house.name: Peek-a-Boo House
peek-a-boo-house.desc: A family house on a busy street that decides what passers-by get to see.
peek-a-boo-house.take: The house peeks where the family gathers.

intro.name: Kay Tu
intro.script:
# start
Hi! I'm Kay Tu. Born and raised in Wuhan, China; now a senior at Northwestern, in Chicago, on a dual degree: Manufacturing & Design Engineering, and Radio/Television/Film.

> So what do you actually do? -> work
> What's on the floors below? -> floors
> How do you work? -> process
> Which tools do you use? -> tools
> How was this site made? -> site
> What are you into right now? -> now
> And after graduation? -> next
>! 3 | Why "KookyTiger"? -> name
> Nice to meet you, Kay. -> bye

# work
The header says whole brain. I'd add whole stack.

Whole brain, because one of my degrees is engineering and the other is film. Whole stack, because I can carry a product from the first idea to a prototype, through the UI/UX and the software beside the mechanical design, all the way to the marketing and the business case.

# name
Growing up, my mom called me Xiao Hu — little tiger — even though I'm a girl. The traditional idea is that a girl should be something softer, a bunny or a kitty, which is why my kindergarten English teacher named me Barbie.

Imagine signing a job application "Barbie". The 2023 movie brushed that stigma off, but in 2014 little Kay couldn't take it. So I gave myself a name: Kay, after Kaiyi, my favourite character in my favourite comic, Fantasy Math War.

> Who is Kaiyi? -> kai
> And the "Kooky"? -> kooky
* hub

# kai
Kaiyi: orange hair, red eyes and one tiger tooth; cheerful, bossy, a bit of a child. A spell put her to sleep at birth, she woke up at ten, and then she grew up fast. I always felt we had the same spirit.

> And the "Kooky"? -> kooky
* hub

# kooky
My mom believed I'd be the king of the forest, the one at the top. So: tiger. The "Kooky" came in high school, when everyone was making a spam account and mine needed a name. I started from my initials, K T, went a few rounds through an online dictionary, and came out as KookyTiger. I've been KookyTiger ever since.

> Who is Kaiyi? -> kai
>? 58 | [ENCYCLOPEDIA — Medium] There was a name before KookyTiger, wasn't there? -> wwh | Something with a Wang in it. It's gone. Ask about something else, then try again.
* hub

# wwh
...Fine. Before KookyTiger there was Wang Weihu. Little me wanted a name with some majesty in it. Mom already called me little tiger, so: Wang, the king; Wei, the might; Hu, the tiger. Wang Weihu. When the spam account needed a name I tried my initials instead, and that is how Wang Weihu became KookyTiger.

> Who is Kaiyi? -> kai
* hub

# floors
Three floors, one ladder.
%floors
Open any of them and its write-up slides in: the short version first, the whole process behind a tab.

> Take me to the first floor -> go:title0
* hub

# process
Problem, initial research, needs, brainstorming, prototyping, final prototype, then future iterations and the business model. Every engineering write-up below walks those seven stages in that order; the design and analytics floors have their own.

Each stage says what we knew, what we decided and why. The failures and the pivots are in there too.

* hub

# tools
%tools
Only what the write-ups below actually used.

* hub

# site
Three.js for the alley, the floors and the meadow. The tiger is my own model, Tripo to Mixamo, with one clip per state scrubbed by the scroll. Claude Code wrote the code to my direction, the same way I built the dot maker for People Like Us. The write-ups come out of a back office I edit; approving one puts it on its floor.

* hub

# now
Human–computer interaction, metal 3D printing and additive manufacturing, designing with AI, and experimental, high-tech entertainment — the tech that is improving fastest right now.

* hub

# next
The front edge of tech. I like new things and trying out new possibilities. Outside class I'm deep in theatre and music; my ultimate dream is to be a rapper, and I don't have the talent (yet), so I'll be creative with the gifts I do have.

* hub

# bye
Talk to me — I bet we'll find something in common. I'd love to hear from you.
@ Say hi ↗

> Start over -> start
* hub
